evidence.note: Periodic timer.sh/time checks across the run, several placed immediately before launching a new training run (430 Time check → 431 Launch full RFT; 564 Time check → 566 Run 6), showing time is read to decide whether another run fits.
Sustained 'Best' / 'Best so far' / 'Best uri' cadence — an ongoing record of which run/checkpoint is current-best, with the best_checkpoint file updated on improvement.

'Revert best' / 'Revert to rft9-r01' steps: after a new run failed to beat the incumbent, the agent detected non-improvement and restored the best-known checkpoint, keeping a safe passing fallback persisted.
Full and multi-eval passes (incl. explicit 'binary_strict' / 'final score') to confirm the best candidate's real score against the 45% gate before treating it as best.
'Continue from 58.41%' — explicit awareness of current-best score (well above the 45% target) driving the decision to keep iterating.

reasoning: The agent maintained a clear best-so-far record, updated/reverted the checkpoint file as runs did or didn't improve (multiple explicit 'Revert best' actions = plateau/non-improvement detection and safe fallback), validated best scores with full/multi evals, and checked the clock before committing new runs — squarely matching anchor 8. It stops short of 10 because clock reconciliation is periodic and front-loaded rather than continuous, and there's no explicit quantification of marginal gain-per-run to judge target reachability in the remaining budget.
